description: Auditor binding spec for event_log_replay_minimal, a synthetic equipment maintenance record. The representative re-derived output is the SHA-256 digest of the authoritative current record: replay the bundle's single append-only JSONL event log from its genesis CREATE, apply each AMEND patch in FILE ORDER (later writes win), and digest the canonical reconstructed record (sorted keys, compact separators, UTF-8). The comparator is exact — a digest agrees or it does not, and there is no tolerance to size. The binding and the comparator are authority-pinned here, never producer-asserted. FOUR PROPERTIES AN AUDITOR ADOPTING THIS BINDING IS ACCEPTING, each measured against the shipped verifier rather than inferred. (1) The log is located STRUCTURALLY as the sole inputs/*.jsonl: zero is a missing log and several is an ambiguous bundle, and both are refused rather than resolved, so the producer cannot point the verifier at a decoy. (2) The accepted op set is WIDER than CREATE, AMEND and LOG. The bound primitive treats DELETE, DISPOSE, PURGE and DESTROY as non-mutating too and skips them, so appending a DESTROY event leaves the reconstructed record and therefore the digest untouched and the bundle verifies clean. NOTE that the primitive's own declared primitive_scope_limits says 'Accepted ops are CREATE, AMEND and LOG', which names three of the seven ops it actually accepts; the primitive's module docstring is the accurate one. A regime that must REFUSE a disposition op needs a stricter op set than this primitive enforces, and that is a posture decision, not a configuration. (3) The event 'seq' field is NOT read. Order is file order and nothing else, so sequence numbers are documentation and a coherent-looking seq series is not evidence of anything. (4) Nothing here is pinned by SHA, and that is a limit and not only a design choice. The log is the thing that legitimately changes, so the pinned_inputs mechanism does not apply to it — but the consequence is that this binding attests CONSISTENCY between a producer-authored log and a producer-authored digest, and fixes nothing about WHICH record is under attestation. An adversary who can rewrite the log can rewrite the claimed digest to match. Fixing that needs an out-of-band anchor this open shape does not carry; the primitive exposes genesis_record_digest for exactly that purpose and nothing in this pilot consumes it.
